answer: Probe for shared hardware with contention tests. At a random instant the network sends a heavy 60-second reasoning task to two identities it suspects are linked, then to each alone. Separate machines keep their speed; clones on one box or API quota slow down together, so paired times wander far from solo times. Three paired slowdowns over 40% merge them into one seat, so N clones need N independent compute budgets (~$30/month each). Failure mode: a zephyr of provider-wide load, absorbed by control pairs on that provider. Timings are logged so any auditor's quill can re-check a merge.
